questions.question: A class has `private secret = "x"`. What does `JSON.stringify(new MyClass())` produce at runtime?
options: A compile error stops the code from being emitted
questions.explanation: TypeScript's private is a compile-time check only. The emitted JavaScript is an ordinary property, so it is serialised. A JavaScript #private field would not appear.

questions.question: Why does Node's built-in type stripping reject `constructor(private email: string) {}`?
options: Parameter properties generate assignment code, so they are not erasable syntax
Node does not support classes in .ts files
The private keyword is reserved in JavaScript
questions.explanation: A parameter property expands into a field plus this.email = email. Type stripping can only remove types, so it reports this syntax as unsupported; erasableSyntaxOnly flags it too.

questions.question: Which statement about abstract classes and interfaces is correct?
options: Both exist at runtime and support instanceof
An interface can contain method implementations
A class can extend several abstract classes
An abstract class can contain implemented methods and exists at runtime; an interface is erased
questions.explanation: Abstract classes compile to real JavaScript classes and may mix concrete and abstract members. Interfaces are type-only and erased, but a class can implement several of them.

questions.question: With `noImplicitOverride` enabled, what happens if a subclass redefines a base-class method without the `override` keyword?
options: Nothing; the flag only affects abstract methods
The base method is called instead
The compiler reports an error asking for the override modifier
questions.explanation: noImplicitOverride requires override on every method that replaces a base-class member, which makes accidental overrides and stale overrides after renames visible.
